title: [3/8/2023] Visits to the library and reasons for doing so
prompt: The charts below give information about the number of people who use public libraries and the main reasons to visit in Britain in 1991 and in 2000. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The pie charts provide data on the primary reasons why people visited public libraries in the UK in 1991 and 2000.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, libraries received the same number of visitors in both years, with borrowing and returning books being the most common purpose. However, a shift was observed in the way users utilized these facilities, as borrowing or returning videos, which was not present in 1991, and seeking information emerged as significant reasons by the end of the period shown.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: In 1991, nearly two-thirds of visits to British public libraries were to borrow or return books, which was considerably higher than the next most common purpose, reading newspapers or magazines, with only 15% of visits. Both of these categories witnessed a 10% drop by 2000, standing at 55% and 5% respectively. A similar downward trend was recorded in studying, as it accounted for 10% of all visits in 1991, but declined significantly to a mere 2% in 2000.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: On the other hand, there was a corresponding rise in the popularity of obtaining information, with its share doubling from 10% to 20% in the latter year. Meanwhile, while no visitors borrowed videos from libraries in 1991, nearly one-fifth did so in 2000, making it the third most prevalent reason. Finally, public libraries in the uk received the same number of visits in both years, at 290 million.
